idiom_name: Array.prototype.filter with a typed predicate / type guard (`x is T`)
implementation_notes: The runtime operation is the same built-in as JavaScript, but TypeScript's realization is the predicate type: a guard signature such as `(m): m is PriceMessage => m.kind === 'price'` filters and narrows the result type at once, whereas a plain boolean predicate leaves the union intact and forces casts. Async message feeds get the same treatment inside an async generator (`for await (const m of src) if (keep(m)) yield m`) or an observer pipeline, and criteria loaded from configuration are parsed once into such a predicate. A filter class is not idiomatic - export a named, pure predicate instead.
pitfalls: A predicate returning `boolean` does not narrow the element type - only an `x is T` guard (or an assertion signature) does, so a plain callback still forces casts or unsafe member access.

filter always allocates a new array; on a hot loop prefer a for-loop or an async generator, and remember the filtered copy no longer shares the union's exhaustiveness guarantees unless the guard narrowed it.
The callback receives (value, index, array): a predicate that declares a second parameter silently receives the index, which only fails to compile when the types differ.
